summary: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts have concluded their science mission aboard the International Space Station and are preparing for their return journey to Earth. In civil space management and research, NASA has opened applications for its next class of flight directors, selected a team to explore concepts for targeting a potential lunar cave, and successfully demonstrated thermal protection capabilities for its upcoming DAVINCI Venus probe. Within military space and national defense, the U.S. Navy inked a $24.4 billion contract with Raytheon to accelerate SM-6 missile production, the Pentagon partnered with CIA-backed venture firm In-Q-Tel for technology scouting, and the Department of Defense Space Policy office experienced a key leadership departure. In physical and space science developments, the Department of Energy announced $400 million for frontier research, while new academic findings highlighted the discovery of the lowest-mass double neutron star system found to date, modeled the physical behavior of water on the moon, and suggested through simulations that the Milky Way formed from thousands of smaller early galaxies. Looking ahead, space operations move into high gear next week as the Space Development Agency prepares to launch 21 additional data transport satellites into orbit.
